name: KUTCH ROGAN PAINTED TEXTILE
material: Tussar Silk with Castor Oil & Natural Mineral Pigments
craft_technique: Freehand trailing of thick castor paste via metal stylus onto folded textile
traditional_use: Bridal ghaghras, ceremonial wall hangings (pari-karan), and auspicious gift drapes for royal and pastoral Maldhari families.
cultural_significance: One of India's rarest endangered crafts, preserved by a single artisan family in Nirona village using castor oil boiled for 48 hours to create elastic paint.
associated_practice: Rogan mirror-symmetry folding technique and bridal trousseau preparation.
contributor: Rizwan Khatri, Master Rogan Artist, Nirona

dimensions.validation_notes: Textile planar depth below laser scanner tolerance; measured by optical rule.

texture.value: Embossed rubbery filigree adhered to fabric weave

shape.value: Rectangular wall hanging with central Tree of Life motif

oral_knowledge.speaker: Rizwan Khatri
oral_knowledge.transcript: રોગન કળામાં એરંડીના તેલને બે દિવસ ઉકાળીને જે લુગદી બને છે, તેને હથેળીમાં ગરમ કરીને સળી વડે કાપડ પર દોરો ખેંચવામાં આવે છે. આખી દુનિયામાં માત્ર અમારા નિરોણા ગામમાં આ કળા જીવંત છે.
oral_knowledge.translation: In Rogan art, castor oil is boiled for two days into a dense paste. Master artisans warm it on the palm and draw fine thread-like paint filaments using a metal stylus without touching the fabric. This rare heritage survives exclusively in our Nirona village.

cultural_origin.name: Nirona Village, Kutch, Gujarat
cultural_origin.details: The sole surviving global center of freehand Rogan textile art.

provenance.action: Completed 120-hour freehand Tree of Life composition.
